$comment: Riftlight, Restless Coast strand end (docs/campaigns/continental-rift/arc.md, bone-yard; design note bone-yard-review.md). Rewritten in November 2026 as the pilot for the whole-campaign rewrite. Question: whose ruins are these, and why did they land here? Puddle, the Skupper guide, carries it; Pip Thistledown voices Lady Olivia's ideas. The p1 (same_stone) is that the ruins' carvings match the buried bridge. Sets no journey flag; reads fragment_paths_learned / fragment_sky_learned only to point at the convergence.
title: The Borrowed Ruins

plate.narration: At the edge of the Bone Yard, broken stone walls stand among enormous pale arches. Salt wind moves through the gaps. A narrow path curves between the quiet ruins.

goal.text: Whose ruins are these, and why did they land here?

steps.label: Cross the bone field to the ruins
Read the carvings on the ruins
Get past the crawlers at the tear

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny and a little spooky, with real consequences. Short sentences. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel. The bones are tired, not angry; nobody dies.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.saltrot_guide: Puddle, the Skupper guide (she/her). Quick, chatty and cheerfully blunt. Guides from brackish pools and channels and signals with her tall crest; puffs up round when startled. Fits exactly in a puddle, hence the name. Keeps her lunch in a floating box. Wants her channel back and to know whose ruins have landed on it.
npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Young manticore scout (he/him). Eager, notebook always out, quotes "Lady Olivia says..." and tries her ideas. Wants a sample to impress her. Kind underneath; changes his mind when the party gives him a reason.

arrival.narration: Past the Saltrot flats, the mud turns pale with bones. This is the Bone Yard. Giant ribs rise from the channels, taller than houses, and between them sit stone ruins that were not here yesterday. A Skupper pops up in a pool. "Puddle!" she says. "Your guide, in case the mud ate your memory. It eats boots." She points a fin. "Those ruins landed on my channel last night. Whose ruins are these? Why did they land here? Help me find out before my pool dries up."

choices.label: Ask Puddle about the Bone Yard

rule.narration: Puddle flicks a pebble onto a bone. It wobbles, rolls back uphill, and drops into her pool. Plop. "Bone Yard rule," she says. "Take nothing, hum something, and leave before the tide turns. Whatever you take comes back. Usually in your boot." The ruins stand across a field of bones and channels. "I only go where it's wet. How do you want to cross?"

check_rib.narration: The rib is as wide as a bench and as long as a street. It is also slimy. Puddle swims along underneath. "Arms out," she calls. "Like a heron."
check_rib.prompt: Run the whole slippery rib without falling off

onSuccess.narration: You run it like a balance beam and hop down at the far end. From up there you spotted a flicker of light deep in the ruins, like a candle in a window.

onFailure.narration: Halfway along, your feet go one way and the rest of you goes the other. You slide down into a heap of old bone shells. Crunch. Only your pride breaks, and a little skin.

check_wade.narration: The channel is low and getting lower. Puddle swims ahead, then turns. "Mud's thick here. Lean in and push. If you stop, it keeps you."
check_wade.prompt: Push through the sticky channel beside Puddle

onSuccess.narration: You push through, one squelch at a time. Puddle cheers every step like a race. Near the ruins the water is only ankle deep. "They're drinking my channel," she mutters.

onFailure.narration: The mud grabs both legs and holds on. Puddle puffs up round as a ball, and you grab her like a float. She tows you out. "Ow. Spines. Sorry." You are free, and one arm tingles where she poked.

fly_over.narration: Your griffin flaps up over the bones. From the sky, the ruins make a broken ring with a flicker of light in the middle, like a candle in a window. You glide back down. Puddle swims up, out of breath. "Show-off," she says, delighted.

skull.narration: The path runs under a skull as big as a barn. Nobody knows what it belonged to, and Puddle says nobody should dig to find out. Inside it is cool and smells of salt. A crab lives in its nose and glares at you. "Speak low," Puddle whispers from a channel. "The bones aren't angry. They're tired."

ruins_edge.narration: Little pale creatures clatter along the foot of the ruins, in shells made of old bone chips, like coats covered in buttons. Bone crawlers. They all hurry toward a flicker of light deep inside. Then one stops and sniffs your pack, where the Listening Chime hums. "Uh oh," says Puddle. "Crawlers love fresh magic. Your chime hums like a kettle."

choices.label: Hold the chime still and sneak

check_hum.narration: You hum low and steady. Puddle hums along from her channel, very loudly and a little flat.
check_hum.prompt: Hum so the chime's buzz hides inside your tune

onSuccess.narration: The chime's buzz melts into your tune. The crawler waves a leg, puzzled, and clatters off after the others.

onFailure.narration: Your hum wobbles into a squeak. The crawler loves it. It falls in behind you, clicking happily.

sneak.narration: Hold the chime still in both hands. The crawlers look up, then down, then up again. Move only while they look down. Puddle flicks her crest to help you count.

interaction.cue: Step while the crawlers look down.

onSuccess.narration: Not one rattle. The crawler sniffs the air, gives up, and hurries after the others.

onFailure.narration: A loose chip skitters under your foot. The crawler spins around and falls in behind you, clicking happily.

onAssisted.narration: Puddle flicks her crest each time they look down, and you all step together. Not one rattle.

lullaby.narration: Your songkeeper sings, soft and slow. The crawler sways. Then it tucks in its legs and falls asleep right there in the path, snoring like a tiny rattle. "I'm telling my grandmother about that," says Puddle.

crawler_tail.narration: The crawler follows you to the ruins, trying to climb into your pack after the chime. At last Puddle opens her floating lunch box and gives it her kelp roll. The crawler wears it as a hat and wanders off, proud. "That," says Puddle, "was my lunch."

ruins_gate.narration: Inside, everything is gray stone with white specks, like salt on bread. A stair climbs into the sky and stops. Puddle hops into a salty puddle the tide left by the gate. It fits her exactly. "Named for it," she says. On a wall sits Pip Thistledown, the young manticore scout, prying at a carved stone with a spoon. "Lady Olivia says a real scout brings back samples!"

pip_chip.narration: The carved chip pops halfway out with a click. Under it, the wall hums, the same buzz as your chime. Puddle's crest folds flat. "Pip. Take nothing. It comes back." "Then I'll only borrow it!" says Pip. "Lady Olivia says you can't learn anything if you're scared of a pebble." What will you do?

choices.label: Talk to him, manticore to manticore

check_pip.narration: Pip hugs the chip like a prize. But he keeps glancing at Puddle.
check_pip.prompt: Convince Pip that a drawing is a better sample than a stone

onSuccess.narration: Pip sighs and pushes the chip back. It clicks into place by itself, like a puzzle piece going home. Pip jumps. "Did it just pull?"

onFailure.narration: "A drawing can't hum," says Pip, and he keeps the chip.

manticore_talk.narration: You flick your tail the polite manticore way, low and slow. Pip's ears go pink. "Okay, okay," he mutters, and pushes the chip back. It clicks into place by itself, like a puzzle piece going home.

pip_draws.narration: Pip draws the chip instead, tongue out, with a lot of shading. "For Lady Olivia," he says. "And maybe Master Orin. He likes drawings." Puddle's crest pops back up.

pip_keeps.narration: Pip tucks the chip into his pocket and pats it. The pocket hums. Puddle says nothing, very loudly. Deep in the ruins, a crawler stops, and turns its head toward Pip.

explore.narration: The ruins are a maze of walls with no roofs. "I can't see over them from down here," says Puddle. "Somebody tell me what this place is." Pip points his spoon two ways at once. Where will you look?

check_stair.narration: The stair has no rail and no top. Each step is worn in the middle, smooth as soap.
check_stair.prompt: Climb the wobbly stair to the very top step

onSuccess.narration: You reach the top step and hold on to the sky. Pip cheers from below.

onFailure.narration: The stair wobbles. You come down a lot faster than you went up, straight through a doorway.

check_doors.narration: Every doorway looks the same. Some have dust. Some have crawler tracks. One smells very old, like a cupboard nobody has opened.
check_doors.prompt: Pick the doorway that holds something, and not somebody

onSuccess.narration: You pick the dusty one with no tracks. Good choice.

onFailure.narration: You pick the one with the most tracks. Bad choice.

stair_top.narration: From the top, the ruins make a ring of walls around an open square, like a town square that lost its town. Its gate faces north, upriver. In the middle, the flicker of light shivers, and crawlers circle it. "What do you see?" Pip calls up. "Is it treasure?"

doorway_step.narration: Inside the oldest doorway, the front step is worn into a dip by feet, a long, long time ago. Somebody went in and out of this door every day. Pip takes off his hat. "Somebody lived here," he whispers.

doorway_nest.narration: Wrong doorway. It is full of sleeping crawlers, packed like spoons in a drawer. They wake up grumpy and pour out past your ankles, clattering off toward the middle of the ruins. One nips Pip's tail on the way. "Rude," says Pip.

carvings.narration: Puddle calls you back to her puddle. "Low down by the gate. Old carving. Copy it for me, I can't reach." Under the moss is a row of shapes cut into the stone. Watch them, then draw them in order.

interaction.cue: Watch the carved shapes, then draw them in order.

onSuccess.narration: Your copy is neat and exact. "Good," says Puddle. "I could read that in the dark."

onFailure.narration: Your copy wobbles. One wave looks like a sausage. But every shape is there.

onAssisted.narration: Puddle calls out each shape from her puddle, and you draw as she talks. The copy comes out neat.

same_stone.narration: You hold your drawing beside the stone and remember the buried bridge. Its old arches were this same gray stone, with these same white specks, curved this same way. They had this same waterline, carved high up. These ruins and that bridge came from the same old place. Something carried them both away and set them down far apart. "The bridge has family," Puddle whispers.

lean.narration: A wave touches the walls. Every stone creaks, and the whole ruin leans a finger's width north, upriver. Your chime swings the same way, toward the glacier far away, and hums. Pip, who has climbed a wall for a better look, wobbles. "They're trying to walk home!" "Moved things do that," says Puddle. "Goats. Ruins. Everything wants home."

catch_pip.narration: The wall tips under Pip's feet. His spoon goes one way and Pip goes the other.
catch_pip.prompt: Catch Pip before he lands in Puddle's puddle

onSuccess.narration: You catch him by the scruff, like a kitten. Pip dangles and blinks. "Thank you. That was very scientific of you."

onFailure.narration: He lands on you, and then you both land in Puddle's puddle. Puddle puffs up in surprise, and you get stung a little. "Sorry, sorry," says Puddle, shrinking.

pip_idea.narration: Pip's eyes shine. "If ruins can walk, Lady Olivia could make them walk anywhere! Bridges where we need them. A tower by the sea!" Puddle looks at the leaning stones and says nothing. What do you tell Pip?

choices.label: Maybe they just want to go home

pip_amazing.narration: Pip writes AMAZING in his notebook and underlines it three times. Puddle's crest droops a little. "Things you push," she says, "push back."

choices.label: Follow the lean to the middle

pip_home.narration: Pip chews his pencil. Then he writes "Ask the ruins?" in his notebook and draws a very small question mark. Puddle's crest stands up tall.

choices.label: Follow the lean to the middle

dam.narration: A fallen arch lies across Puddle's channel like a lid on a pot. Water piles up behind it. Past it, in an open square, a tear in the air flickers: bigger, smaller, bigger. Crawlers crowd around it. "Shoving is quick," says Puddle. "But stones scrape, and shoved things creep back. Or we help it go the way it leans. That's slow, and the tear keeps growing."

variants.text: Pip is already rolling up his sleeves. "Lady Olivia would shove it."
Pip scratches his ear. "Or we could ask it. Can you ask an arch?"

choices.label: Shove the arch out of the way
Help it go the way it leans
Let your bigfoot lift it out

check_shove.narration: Everyone grabs an edge. Pip grabs Puddle's tail by mistake. "Not that," says Puddle. "On three!"
check_shove.prompt: Shove the fallen arch out of the channel together

onSuccess.narration: The arch grinds over the rocks and flops out of the channel.

onFailure.narration: The arch tips, cracks in two, and half of it thumps right back into the channel.

shoved.narration: Water rushes through with a happy gurgle, and Puddle shoots past you like a cork. "Water!" Then she sees the arch. Its carved face scraped along the rocks. The waterline is gone, ground into gray dust. And already, with every wave, the arch creaks back toward the channel.

variants.text: Good thing you drew it first, and neatly.
Good thing you drew it first, sausage wave and all.

cracked.narration: Only a trickle gets past the broken half. Puddle's crest droops. "Well. That was loud." The carving is in crumbly pieces now. Pip pats the arch. "Sorry," he tells it. In the square, at least, the tear is still small.

variants.text: Good thing you drew it first, and neatly.
Good thing you drew it first, sausage wave and all.

bigfoot_lift.narration: Your bigfoot hugs the arch and stands up. It comes away with a groan and a lot of dripping. "Water!" cries Puddle, and shoots past like a cork. But the carved face scraped as it came up, and the waterline is gone. Already the arch creaks back toward the channel.

variants.text: Good thing you drew it first, and neatly.
Good thing you drew it first, sausage wave and all.

watch_lean.narration: Puddle lies flat in the trickle and watches the waves. "It leans the same way every time," she says. "Scoop the mud from the right places, in the right order, and the water will push it for us." She whispers a different part of the plan to each of you.

interaction.cue: Put Puddle's scooping plan in order.
clues: Start on the side it leans toward.
The keystone comes right after the north side.
Finish at the far corner, where the water wants out.

onSuccess.narration: Wave by wave, you scoop. Wave by wave, the arch slides.

onFailure.narration: You scoop the keystone first. The arch leans back, sulking, and Puddle has to start again.

onAssisted.narration: Pip reads the clues out loud, and you scoop together, in order.

nudged.narration: The arch slides north, a little at a time, the way it wanted to go. The water curls around it and runs free, and the carving is still whole. "It went where it wanted," says Puddle, swimming a loop. Then she stops. While you worked, the tear grew wide and bright, and more crawlers came.

nudged_slow.narration: At last the arch slides, but only a trickle gets past. "The tide will finish it," says Puddle. "By morning, it runs." The carving is still whole. But while you worked, the tear grew wide and bright, and more crawlers came.

court_quick.narration: You step into the square. The tear hangs in the air like a crack in a window, small and flickering. The crawlers circle it, clattering. Then they all turn at once, toward your humming chime.

variants.text: And toward Pip's humming pocket. They pile around him against the far wall. "I would like to give this back now!" squeaks Pip.
Puddle bobs in the channel at the edge of the square. "Watch my crest. Up means duck!"
Puddle calls from the trickle outside. "Watch my crest over the wall. Up means duck!"

court_grown.narration: You step into the square. The tear is wide now, bright as a window at night, and it flickers bigger and smaller. More crawlers circle it, clattering. Then they all turn at once, toward your humming chime.

variants.text: And toward Pip's humming pocket. They pile around him against the far wall. "I would like to give this back now!" squeaks Pip.
Puddle bobs in the channel at the edge of the square. "Watch my crest. Up means duck!"
Puddle calls from the trickle outside. "Watch my crest over the wall. Up means duck!"

fight_quick.narration: Close the tear by ending two turns beside it, or drive the crawlers off. Loose stones by the tear bite anyone who stops on them.

fight_quick_pip.narration: Close the tear by ending two turns beside it, or drive the crawlers off. Loose stones by the tear bite anyone who stops on them. Pip is stuck in the pile by the far wall. End a turn next to him to pull him out.

fight_grown.narration: Close the tear by ending three turns beside it, or drive the crawlers off. Loose stones by the tear bite anyone who stops on them.

fight_grown_pip.narration: Close the tear by ending three turns beside it, or drive the crawlers off. Loose stones by the tear bite anyone who stops on them. Pip is stuck in the pile by the far wall. End a turn next to him to pull him out.

court_after.narration: The last crawler clatters off into the ruins. The square is yours.

variants.text: The tear folds shut like a sleepy eye. With the fresh magic gone, the crawlers lose interest. Soon they are back to fitting their shells, one bone chip at a time.
Behind them, the tear still flickers, bigger, smaller, bigger. "We'll mark it," says Puddle. "Travelers go around it from now on."
Pip tumbles out of the pile, hugging the chip. "Thank you," he gasps. "This chip is much more popular than me."
Pip squeezes out on his own, scratched and grumpy. The crawlers kept his notebook. "My drawings for Lady Olivia," he moans.

puddle_court.narration: Puddle swims right into the square, the first Skupper ever to see it from inside. She touches a carved waterline with one fin. "Same as the bridge," she says softly. "I had to see it myself."

variants.text: Puddle can't reach the square over dry stone. So Pip lifts her up to the wall, very carefully, because of the spines. She peeks over at a carved waterline. "Same as the bridge," she says softly. "I had to see it myself."
Then she looks back at the scraped arch, and sighs.

swarmed.narration: The crawlers pile on, all reaching for your humming chime. "Out! Out!" cries Puddle, crest straight up. You hold the chime tight and back out of the square. Your drawing slips from your pack, and three crawlers sit on it at once. The short way through the square is theirs now.

variants.text: Pip wriggles out behind you. The crawlers kept his notebook.
Pip stumbles out beside you, hugging the chip.

float_out.narration: Puddle puffs up round as a ball. Everyone grabs a spine, carefully. She floats you down her channel, out of the square and around the swarm. "Ow," she says, the whole way. "Ow. Ow. You're welcome."

check_rim.narration: The wall-tops are narrow and crumbly, high above the square. Below, the crawlers clatter and watch your chime.
check_rim.prompt: Hurry along the crumbly wall-tops without dropping into the square

onSuccess.narration: Step, step, hop. You reach the far side, the long way around. The crawlers lose sight of the chime and go back to their tear.

onFailure.narration: A stone gives way. You drop into a dry ditch one hop from the swarm, then scramble out the far side, scraped and puffing. It is the long way around, and it was longer than you hoped.

rest.narration: Puddle opens her floating lunch box: kelp rolls in leaves. "Guides eat first," she says, and eats one, then shares the rest. Pip eats his in one bite. The ruins creak north with every wave. "Rule says leave before the tide turns," says Puddle. "But I've always wanted to see them move."

variants.text: Puddle's lunch box is empty, because a crawler is wearing her lunch. So Pip shares his emergency crackers. They taste a bit like map. The ruins creak north with every wave. "Rule says leave before the tide turns," says Puddle. "But I've always wanted to see them move."

hurry_out.narration: Puddle leads the way back, pool to pool, crest high. Behind you, water is already sliding into the channels.
hurry_out.prompt: Hop the bones back to the flats before the water rises

onSuccess.narration: Dry boots, all of you. Puddle is very impressed, and says so twice.

onFailure.narration: The last channel fills before you reach it. Water slides in on both sides, and the flats are on the other side of it.

cut_off.narration: "Stand still," says Puddle. She swims out to the deepest part and puffs up round as a ball. One at a time, you hold her spines, carefully, and she ferries you across. "Ow. Next. Ow. Next." By the last trip her crest is drooping, and you are wet to the knees.

watch_tide.narration: You stay. The tide slides in, and every stone creaks. The whole ruin leans north, and for one breath its gate points straight upriver, toward the buried bridge far away. "Look," Puddle breathes. Then cold water swirls around your knees.

check_tide.narration: The water is rising fast and pulling hard. Pip climbs onto Puddle's head, which she does not enjoy.
check_tide.prompt: Wade out through the rising tide, holding on to each other

onSuccess.narration: You wade out, slow and steady, arm in arm. Nobody lets go.

onFailure.narration: The water knocks your feet away. Puddle puffs up, and you ride out on her like a spiky raft.

tide_turns.narration: At the edge of the Bone Yard, something rattles in your boot. You tip it out: a tiny bone chip. It rolls away by itself, uphill, back toward the ruins. Puddle grins. "Told you. Boot."

variants.text: Then Pip yelps. His pocket is wriggling. The carved chip climbs out, hops down the path, and rolls all the way back to its wall. Pip stares at his empty pocket. "Lady Olivia never said they come back by themselves."
Pip checks his pockets, just in case. Only his drawing. "Drawings don't climb," he says, relieved.

choices.label: Sit with Puddle one last time

drawing.narration: Puddle and Pip both look at your drawing of the carving. "Guides keep an account of everything that comes and goes here," says Puddle. "This belongs in it." "Master Orin and Lady Olivia need to see it!" says Pip. Who should keep it?

variants.text: Your drawing is still under three crawlers, but you remember every shape: a long line, two little waves, a ring. "Guides keep an account of everything that comes and goes here," says Puddle. "Tell it to me, for the account." "Tell it to me, for Master Orin and Lady Olivia!" says Pip. Who should hear it first?

to_puddle.narration: Puddle tucks the drawing into her floating lunch box, where it stays dry. "Every guide on the Saltrot will know this mark by next tide," she says. "If Master Orin wants it, he can come and ask nicely." Pip looks at his feet, then nods. "That's fair."

variants.text: Puddle scratches the shapes into the mud with one fin, then copies them onto a flat shell for the guides' account. "Every guide on the Saltrot will know this mark by next tide," she says. Pip looks at his feet, then nods. "That's fair."

to_pip.narration: Pip tucks the drawing inside his scarf and hugs it. "Lady Olivia will know what to do with it," he says. "Maybe she can move ruins too!" Puddle's crest folds flat. "Tell her," she says slowly, "that these ones want to go home."

variants.text: Pip says the shapes over and over, so he won't forget: line, wave, wave, ring. "Lady Olivia will know what to do with it," he says. "Maybe she can move ruins too!" Puddle's crest folds flat. "Tell her," she says slowly, "that these ones want to go home."
Pip stops. "I'll show Master Orin too," he decides. "He'll want to ask the ruins things first."

ending.narration: Puddle swims beside you as far as the water goes. "Old Ossley, the frog boatman, takes his ferry upriver on the next tide," she says. "I checked his channel myself." So here is your piece: the buried bridge and these ruins came from the same old place, and something carried them apart. Something is moving the land. What is it? And can you put things right?

variants.text: Behind you, Puddle's channel runs clear around the arch, and it will stay that way.
Behind you, Puddle's channel trickles around the arch. By morning it will run.
Behind you, the shoved arch is creeping back toward Puddle's channel. "Then I'll shove it again," she sighs. "Every tide. Forever. Fine."
Behind you, half of the cracked arch still sits in Puddle's channel. She will be wading around it for a long time.
The short way through the square belongs to the crawlers, for now.
Somewhere upriver, Pip is running to find the Riftseekers with the carving.
The tear still flickers in the square, so Puddle will guide travelers around it.
You carry another piece too. Master Orin Vale will want to lay them side by side.
You carry another piece too. Master Orin Vale will want to lay them side by side.
